pages.lesson:
LESSON: WRITING 5.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING: CREATIVE LANGUAGE

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing: Creative language

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing: Creative language
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: How do we develop good handwriting?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify aspects of creative language in texts based on the theme for fluency
2. write texts based on the theme neatly and legibly for effective communication
3. appreciate creativity and handwriting in effective communication

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing: Creative language

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing: Creative language

Teach
• Focus skill: identify aspects of creative language in texts based on the theme for fluency.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing: Creative language.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing: Creative language
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we develop good handwriting?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
